reviews.outcome: No serious defect established in these adopted passages. The corpus states freshness explicitly for both finite prescribed sets, includes empty sides and repeated tuple coordinates in the m,n schema, and proves shared-syntax quantifier elimination through specified finite maps. Kruckman's weaker displayed schema also gives fresh witnesses by finite padding; its omitted explicit inequalities are not a false assertion. Probability and the zero-one law are outside this entry.

reviews.checked_passages: Printed p.27, Proposition7.5 and Theorem7.6(i)–(ii), singleton/finite automorphism-orbit characterizations of closure, with the surrounding monster-model context.
reviews.outcome: No new serious defect found in these adopted claims. The corpus avoids an unstated monster context by proving the results for a countable omega-saturated model over a finite parameter set, and explicitly extracts a finite conjunction over the original parameters rather than treating an arbitrary type orbit as definable.

reviews.consumers: Root eight-entry execution plan: strongly minimal models classified by dimension.
reviews.outcome: The source works in a monster model. The corpus must replace that assumption with a proved algebraic partial-elementary-map extension lemma using finitely many candidates, then a Zorn back-and-forth extension of the specified basis bijection. Categoricity is stated for infinite kappa strictly above max(language size,aleph0), with existence from the existing exact model-size theorem. No arbitrary prescribed dimension-existence, field/vector-space prerequisite, or saturation criterion is adopted.

reviews.outcome: The corpus replaces the source monster-model setting by arbitrary-domain partial elementary maps, finite/cofinite transport and a finite-candidate algebraic extension lemma. Chain unions and Zorn extend the specified independent-basis bijection to an actual isomorphism of the given models. Classification compares existing dimensions; categoricity and model existence use the strict language-size threshold and the earlier exact model-size theorem. Pure equality shows that prescribed finite dimensions need not occur. No saturation or arbitrary dimension-existence premise is assumed.
